findings.text: When the lexer is at EOF, errorf and errorPrevLine do `pos.Line--` without checking that the line is above 1. For single-line input with no trailing newline, such as `x = "abc` (unterminated string), the error gets Line 0. `ParseError.Error()` then reports "line 0". `ErrorWithPosition` indexes `lines[pe.Position.Line-1]`, which is `lines[-1]`, and panics.

`column()` uses `pos+ll >= Start`, which is off by one. An error that starts at the first byte of a line (Start == pos+ll) is attributed to the previous line. The column becomes len(prevLine)+1, and the caret is drawn far to the right of the real position.

The Len==1 branch prints `col+1` but the else branch prints `col` as the start column. Column numbering is therefore inconsistent: a one-byte error at byte 0 reports column 1, while a multi-byte error at byte 0 reports column 0.

1.reason: In column(), line i covers bytes pos..pos+ll-1, so when Start == pos+ll (the first byte of the next line) the `>=` check still matches line i and gives col = ll; the column and caret are then one past the end of the previous line, a separate bug from the lexer's EOF line handling.

2.reason: column() returns a 0-based offset, but the Len==1 branch prints col+1 while the multi-byte branch prints col, so the same start byte is reported as column 1 in one case and column 0 in the other.
